sources.note: Ran the hybrid+EV filter (37 results across 2 pages) and a second all-fuel pass narrowed to the efficient-gas model list and sorted by mileage ascending (2 pages). Most cars here also appear on CarGurus; credited to whichever source had the better price or richer data.

Richest source by far - tile data carries VIN, EPA combined mpg, deal rating, price-vs-market delta and days-on-market. Ran three passes: hybrid (96 results, 5 pages), electric (10 results) and gasoline filtered to minMpg=32 + maxMileage=110k (78 results, 3 pages).

Ran the generic hybrid query (56 results) plus a combined OR query across prius|leaf|volt|insight|ioniq|niro and the efficient-gas models (185 results). Heavily polluted by buy-here-pay-here dealers reposting down-payment figures as prices - those were screened out.

Logged in and searched hybrid, prius, nissan leaf, chevy volt, volt (retried), corolla, honda civic and camry hybrid, scrolling 5x per query. Real results returned, but almost everything was 110k-210k miles. Yesterday's $3,999 2012 Volt turns out to have 212,000 miles - dropped.
Hybrid browse under $10k returns nothing; cheapest hybrid nationally is a 2025 Kia Niro LX at $24,590. No sub-$10k inventory of any fuel type.
Buy-It-Now hybrid search with zip 80015 / 100 mi returned 65 rows but the radius filter is not honoured - sellers were Glendale CA, Gaffney SC and similar. Zero listings inside Colorado.
Prius query returned 13 local listings. Only one is credible on mileage; the rest are 120k-307k miles.

Sorted national inventory by price ascending. Only two cars under $10k exist: a 2021 Ford EcoSport SE at $8,455 in Oklahoma City (486 mi) and another at $8,599 in San Francisco (963 mi). Both are ~27 mpg SUVs, so they fail the mpg floor anyway.

Searched the Thornton/Denver store sorted by price ascending. Cheapest car in the whole network near 80015 is a 2025 Nissan Leaf S at $17,898; their lowest published filter band is still Under $20k. No sub-$10k cars this run.

Loaded and confirmed 30 Toyota Prius listings under $10k, but all are Utah - roughly 450+ miles from 80015. Excluded on distance; Front Range supply was strong enough this run not to need the stretch.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall-roof compact wagon: excellent overhead clearance when lifting a rear-facing seat in, upright rear bench with easy LATCH access, and the hatch swallows a stroller plus daycare bags.
listings.nextAction: Still the biggest below-market gap on the list at $2,846 under CarGurus market, and it has sat 56 days so there is room to push. Ask for the free Carfax and proof the hybrid battery has never thrown a code, then book a test drive.
listings.why: Holds the top spot for a second run. 40 mpg combined, only 85k miles, the largest below-market delta of any car here, and the newest non-suspect hybrid under $8.5k inside 15 miles. Ford's eCVT hybrid transaxle in this generation has a strong reliability record and only one open recall campaign.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan - the roomiest rear seat in the top five. A rear-facing convertible fits without pushing the front passenger seat forward.
listings.nextAction: PRICE DROPPED $500 since yesterday ($9,398 to $8,898) and it is now $1,709 under market. Move on this one. Ask the dealer to confirm traction-battery warranty status - Hyundai covered it 10yr/100k, so it has just expired at 105k miles.
listings.why: The family pick, and it got $500 cheaper overnight. 5-star NHTSA overall, 40 mpg combined, and a full midsize back seat for under $9k. Hyundai's parallel hybrid uses a conventional 6-speed automatic instead of a CVT, which makes long-term repair simpler and cheaper than a Prius-style transaxle.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a genuinely wide rear bench and easy-to-reach LATCH anchors; verify front-passenger legroom once a rear-facing seat is installed behind it.
listings.nextAction: 78 days on the lot with no deal rating means the dealer has not benchmarked it - bring CarGurus comps. Ask whether Hyundai's 10yr/100k powertrain warranty transferred, and get the recall-completion printout for the 3 open campaigns.
listings.why: Newest car on the whole list at 6 years old with under 60k miles, and 36 mpg combined is the best of any pure-gas car here. Cheapest cost-per-mile of any non-hybrid, and 40,000 fewer miles than anything else near this price.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a flat rear floor and a wide door opening - good for leaning in with a child. Cargo area is shallow but deep enough for a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Ask for a LeafSpy battery-health report (bars remaining and state-of-health percent) before driving out. A 2017 showing 10+ bars covers your 25-mile daycare-and-Sam's-Club loop several times over.
listings.why: Cheapest credible car on the list and the running cost is close to zero - your daily loop is a fraction of even a degraded 2017 Leaf's range, and Level 1 charging overnight is plenty. 2017 is the last of the 30 kWh cars, well past the worst battery-degradation years. Now $579 under market.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact sedan - workable for one rear-facing seat but the front passenger will need to slide forward. Bring your actual car seat to the test drive.
listings.nextAction: NEW today. This is a Mazda2 wearing a Toyota badge - ask for the Carfax and check the rear-seat fit in person, because the cabin is small even though the trunk is a normal sedan trunk.
listings.why: Best pure-gas value found this run: $1,976 under market, 36 mpg combined, and the Mazda-built Skyactiv 1.5 with a conventional 6-speed automatic is one of the most trouble-free small-car drivetrains of its decade - no CVT, no turbo, no timing belt. Sold through Toyota dealers, so parts and service are easy.

listings.carSeatNotes: Same subcompact sedan as the Scion iA above - one rear-facing seat fits, but check front-passenger clearance. Standard low-speed automatic emergency braking is a real plus with a child aboard.
listings.nextAction: NEW today, and the second-lowest mileage on the entire list. It has been listed 114 days at the top of budget, so open at $9,000. Confirm the 3 open recalls are closed out.
listings.why: Only 51,786 miles, a 5-star NHTSA overall rating, and 35 mpg combined - the same Mazda-built drivetrain as the Scion iA but a year newer with 40k fewer miles. Priced right at the ceiling, which is the only reason it is not higher; the 114 days it has sat is your leverage.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan, roomy rear bench and easy LATCH access - one of the better car-seat fits on this list.
listings.nextAction: Private seller - ask for the VIN and a photo of the title before driving out, confirm the one-owner claim on a Carfax, and ask specifically for traction-battery service history.
listings.why: Still the best miles-per-dollar of any hybrid here: 82,500 miles for $7,000 with a one-owner claim, a 5-star crash rating and a real midsize back seat. Private sale means room to negotiate, but it also means you verify everything yourself - no dealer inspection behind it.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a usefully wide rear door aperture; standard all-wheel drive means less drama getting out of an unplowed daycare lot.
listings.nextAction: NEW today. Get the completion records for all 7 open recall campaigns before anything else, and ask whether it has EyeSight automatic emergency braking - the base 2017 2.0i often does not.
listings.why: The only car on the list pairing a 5-star crash rating with standard AWD while still clearing the 32 mpg floor, and it is $1,950 under market. Replaces yesterday's 2018 Impreza hatchback, which the EPA API scored at 31 mpg combined and therefore fails the gas floor - the sedan body is rated 32.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat - the easiest rear-facing install on this list, with wide doors for buckling a toddler in a tight parking spot.
listings.nextAction: Closest car on the list at 4 miles, and it has sat 107 days at $9,995 - open well below asking. Ask for hybrid battery cooling-fan service history; the intake vent behind the rear seat clogs with dust and is the main Camry Hybrid failure mode.
listings.why: The safest bet on the list for a family car. Toyota's hybrid system is the most proven one ever built, 40 mpg combined, only one open recall, and it is 4 miles from home. Price is at the ceiling but 112k miles is mid-life for this drivetrain, and 107 days unsold is real negotiating leverage.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with a roomy back seat; the hybrid battery sits behind the seatback so the trunk is shallower than the gas Fusion - measure your stroller before committing.
listings.nextAction: NEW today and only 3 days on the market at a Great Deal price, 5 miles from home - call this morning. Also listed on Cars.com by AutoNation Ford Arapahoe at the same $7,399.
listings.why: Highest EPA rating of any conventional hybrid on the list at 41 mpg combined, a 5-star crash rating, one open recall, and $1,567 under market five miles from your door. The 124k miles is the only thing holding it back - this drivetrain routinely goes well past 200k, but budget for a battery at some point.

listings.carSeatNotes: Small crossover body on a hatchback footprint: high hip point makes lifting a child in and out of a car seat much easier on your back than any sedan here, and the cargo hold is the biggest on the list.
listings.nextAction: NEW today and it is manufacturer-certified pre-owned, which is unusual under $10k - ask exactly what the CPO warranty still covers and get it in writing. Then ask whether Kia's 10yr/100k hybrid-battery warranty transferred; at 137k miles it has run out either way.
listings.why: 50 mpg combined from a car with real cargo space and a certified pre-owned warranty behind it, for a dollar under budget. The Niro uses a conventional 6-speed dual-clutch rather than a CVT. The 137,754 miles is high - this ranks here rather than top five purely on that, but the CPO inspection offsets some of the risk.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan; the rear bench takes one rear-facing seat but the front passenger will need to move forward.
listings.nextAction: 5-star crash rating at only 60k miles, 11 miles away. Ask for records on the 1.4 turbo's cooling system - water-outlet and thermostat-housing leaks are the known weak point and are cheap to fix if caught early.
listings.why: 34 mpg combined, 5-star NHTSA overall, 60k miles and close to home. Strong all-round value; the 1.4T's coolant-leak history is the only real caveat and a pre-purchase inspection will find it.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall wagon body, easy overhead clearance for lifting a car seat; the plug-in battery eats trunk depth, so measure before committing to a bulky stroller.
listings.nextAction: NEW today and by far the lowest-mileage plug-in on the list. Call before driving 55 miles - confirm it is still there and ask for a battery state-of-health check. A ~21-mile electric range on Level 1 charging covers most of your daily loop.
listings.why: 51,856 miles on a plug-in hybrid for under $10k is genuinely rare - that is 50,000 fewer miles than the other C-Max Energi below and only one open recall against the 2014's eight. The 55-mile drive to Colorado Springs is the trade-off.

listings.carSeatNotes: Tall wagon, easy overhead clearance for a car seat; plug-in battery reduces trunk depth, so measure your stroller.
listings.nextAction: $1,273 under market. Get the completion records for all 8 open recall campaigns and a battery state-of-health check before making the 47-mile trip.
listings.why: A plug-in that could run your commute almost entirely on electricity while keeping a gas engine for road trips - the best of both for this use case, at $1,500 less than the low-mileage 2013 above. The 102k miles and eight open recalls are why it ranks below its newer twin.

listings.carSeatNotes: Full midsize rear seat, very easy rear-facing install; the plug-in battery cuts trunk space to about 10 cubic feet, so a bulky stroller may be a squeeze.
listings.nextAction: Still listed at $8,694 on CarGurus and $7,995 here - use the lower Cars.com price as your anchor and make the dealer honour it. A 29-mile electric range covers your entire daily loop on a regular household outlet.
listings.why: Newest plug-in on the list and the only one whose electric range fully covers the 25-mile workday without ever starting the engine. 5-star crash rating and a midsize back seat. The 127k miles is the reason it is not in the top five.

listings.carSeatNotes: Only four seats - the rear has two buckets split by a battery tunnel. One car seat fits fine; a second child later would not.
listings.nextAction: 5 miles away and a 38-mile electric range covers your commute twice over. Ask for a battery capacity readout and confirm whether the 8yr/100k battery warranty has just expired - at 100,289 miles it is right on the line.
listings.why: Longest electric range of any plug-in here and only a single open recall, with a 5-star crash rating, five miles from home. The four-seat layout and the battery warranty expiring at exactly this mileage are the limiting factors.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan; a single rear-facing seat fits, but check front-passenger clearance once installed.
listings.nextAction: Price ticked down from $8,098 to $8,050. Cars.com still tags the same VIN a Great Deal. Call first and have them email the Carfax and confirm it is on the lot before driving to Colorado Springs.
listings.why: 33 mpg, 5-star crash rating and 70k miles at just over $8k. The 54-mile distance is the only real knock - the nearly identical 2017 Cruze LT at rank 12 is 11 miles away for $900 more and has a nicer trim.

listings.carSeatNotes: Flat-floor hatchback with wide rear doors; SL trim's heated rear seats and heated steering wheel matter on a Colorado winter daycare run because cabin heat is the main range drain.
listings.nextAction: Lowest miles of any car on the list by a wide margin. Worth the 36-mile drive to Boulder, but it is $732 ABOVE market, so get a LeafSpy battery report first and use the delta to negotiate.
listings.why: Only 37,994 miles - nothing else here is close. A 2016 SL is a 30 kWh car, so real-world range comfortably covers the daily loop even with degradation. Ranked here rather than higher because it is priced above market and Leaf values are still softening.

listings.carSeatNotes: The Fit punches far above its size for family duty - the Magic Seat folds flat and upright, the rear doors open wide, and rear legroom is closer to a midsize than a subcompact. One of the best car-seat fits per dollar here.
listings.nextAction: NEW today, 7 miles away, 5-star crash rating. Ask for CVT fluid-service records and get the 4 open recalls confirmed closed.
listings.why: Honda's most practical small car: 34 mpg combined, 5-star NHTSA overall, and a rear seat and cargo hold that embarrass every other subcompact on this list. At 101k miles it is mid-life, and the 1.5 Earth Dreams engine plus CVT is a durable combination if the fluid has been changed.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan with a snug rear seat - workable for one rear-facing seat but tighter than the Elantra or the Fit.
listings.nextAction: Mileage is now disclosed at 91,216 (it was missing yesterday) and the trim is i Touring, not i Sport. Get the Carfax and the completion records for the 6 open recalls.
listings.why: 33 mpg, 5-star crash rating, and Mazda's naturally aspirated 2.0 Skyactiv is one of the most trouble-free engines of its era - no turbo, no direct-injection carbon issues, conventional 6-speed automatic. Seven miles away. The six open recalls are the main thing to clear.

listings.carSeatNotes: The 2020 redesign made the Versa genuinely roomier in back than its price suggests, and it came standard with automatic emergency braking - unusual safety kit at this budget.
listings.nextAction: NEW today. Standard AEB plus a 5-star rating on a 2020 car under $10k is a rare combination. Ask for CVT service records - Nissan's Xtronic is the one component that decides whether this is a bargain.
listings.why: Tied for newest car on the list at six years old, 35 mpg combined, 5-star NHTSA overall and standard automatic emergency braking. The 101,556 miles is high for the year, and the CVT is the known risk, which is why it sits here rather than near the Elantra.

listings.carSeatNotes: Flat-floor hatchback with a wide door opening, same as the newer Leafs, but no heated seats in a 2012 SL's Colorado-spec package - winter cabin heat will hurt range badly.
listings.nextAction: NEW today and the cheapest car on the list. DO NOT buy without a LeafSpy report. A 2012 with a 24 kWh pack that has lost bars may only do 40-50 miles in summer and far less in January - that is still enough for your 25-mile loop, but there is no margin.
listings.why: Cheapest credible car found this run at $4,992 for 74,554 miles, sold by an AutoNation store rather than a corner lot. Listed only as a budget option: a 2012 Leaf is exactly the pre-2017 car the criteria say to screen carefully, and battery health entirely determines whether it is a bargain or a paperweight.

listings.carSeatNotes: Midsize sedan with the largest back seat and trunk of any gas car here - the most comfortable option for a rear-facing seat plus a stroller.
listings.nextAction: Ask for the CVT service history; the 2020 Malibu's continuously variable transmission is the one component worth a dedicated pre-purchase inspection.
listings.why: Newest and roomiest gas car under $10k, only 50,625 miles, one open recall, and it just clears the 32 mpg floor. Take this over the Elantra at rank 3 if back-seat space matters more to you than fuel economy - it costs about $180 a year more in gas.

listings.carSeatNotes: Subcompact - the tightest car-seat fit on this list. Install a rear-facing seat and check the front passenger still has usable legroom before you commit.
listings.nextAction: Private seller right in Aurora - ask for the VIN and a photo of the title before meeting, and arrange the handover somewhere public. It has been listed since mid-July without selling, so the asking price has room.
listings.why: Best fuel economy of any gas-burning car on the list at 50 mpg combined, Toyota hybrid reliability, and it is in your own city. Ranked here only because it is a subcompact with a genuinely tight rear seat and a private sale with no VIN disclosed.

listings.carSeatNotes: Compact sedan; one rear-facing seat fits with the front passenger seat moved forward. Toyota Safety Sense with automatic emergency braking was standard on the 2018 Corolla, which is a real plus.
listings.nextAction: Facebook dealer listing in Aurora - ask for the VIN and the Carfax, and press hard on the '3+ owners' disclosure. At 111k miles and 119 days unsold, $9,900 is too much; a 60k-mile Elantra is the same money.
listings.why: The only Facebook Marketplace car worth listing this run, and it is the closest listing overall at 5 miles. The Eco trim's 32 mpg combined just clears the floor and it has standard AEB plus a 5-star rating. Priced poorly for 111k miles and 3+ owners, which is why it is last on merit rather than higher.

listings.carSeatNotes: Hatchback with a usable rear bench and a large cargo hold - genuinely practical for daycare runs, if the car is real.
listings.nextAction: TREAT AS SUSPECT. A 2022 Prius Prime with 62k miles is a $22,000-$25,000 car; $8,450 is roughly a third of market. Do not wire a deposit, do not accept any shipping or escrow story - insist on seeing the car and the title in person in Denver, and walk away if the seller resists.
listings.why: Carried over from previous runs, still posted at $8,450 and now duplicated across two Craigslist ads. On paper it is the best car on the list - 54 mpg, 5-star, four years old. In practice the price is the classic signature of a fraudulent listing. Included for transparency and so the tracker keeps a record of it, not as a recommendation.
